## Natural history notes

A medium-sized prominent moth characterized by light green to gray-green forewings with subtle darker lines and a soft bark- or leaf-like resting appearance. In Florida, Heterocampa astarte is recorded from the state’s moth fauna and is associated with oak habitats, including hammocks, oak scrub, pine-oak woods, parks, and forest edges where live oaks occur. Adults are mostly nocturnal and may come to lights, while the caterpillars feed on oak foliage, with live oak listed as a preferred host and sand live oak reported as a possible secondary host.
